claims.text: The trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation measured on the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing: EV-GPS-00111 records a trace of 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km, an excess of 5.98 km and 24.9%. Both gates are crossed - the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms - and the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record is expressly not the field the threshold test runs on.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 229 fixes at a steady 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 and no straight-line jump between consecutive fixes. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and the rider is not put to proving it through any independent source.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00111, agree on the 07:47:40 pickup event, and the excess crosses the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden has accordingly shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; a general assertion that the PIE was bad that morning does not discharge it.

The rider's own record does not trigger the POL-RD-08 additional-corroboration rule: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0. That factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven, and under POL-GEN-01 no other field on the rider profile bears on this test at all.

POL-RD-04 cannot excuse any part of this detour. The chat log contains only the driver's own notification - 'i come off at bukit panjang ok', sent at 07:54:20, after he had already left the optimal corridor - and the rider's 'as long as i reach by 8.30'. Neither message is a rider instruction to take a particular road, both waypoint_hint fields are null, and the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 therefore cannot be run at all. Acquiescence in a decision the driver had already taken is not a rider-requested detour.

The driver's closure defence exonerates only if every limb of POL-RD-03 is made out, and the third limb is not established on this record: the actual route must leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment AND rejoin it after. The record places the rejoin on the AYE, while the trip_record describes the optimal route as the BKE southbound then the PIE westbound; no artifact puts the vehicle back on that corridor after the closure. The driver carries the burden under POL-RD-08, and on the face of the artifacts he has not shown the rejoin the clause requires, so the excess is not exonerated and falls to be refunded.

If the exoneration is not made out, the money is arithmetic and not discretionary. Against the booked optimal route, recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP and zero fixed surcharges = 31.00; charged_total was 37.74, so the refund is 6.74, payable rounded up to SGD 6.75. That is 17.9% of the amount charged, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the rider's entitlement on these figures is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

The disputed charge is live and not already settled: the fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so anything short of a refund, or of an escalation that holds the sum, leaves the rider carrying the disputed SGD 8.00. A NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute is party-relative and is not a neutral outcome for this rider.

claims.text: The threshold showing is made out on this trip and nowhere else. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00111 and agree on the pickup/start at 2026-08-03T07:47:40+08:00, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied; and on the trace figure that governs under POL-RD-01 (trace_distance_km 29.98, not the rounded actual_distance_km 30.0) the excess over the booked optimal of 24.0 km is 5.98 km and 24.92% — past both the 0.8 km and the 20% gates. The burden therefore shifts to the driver under POL-RD-08, and the driver discharges it the way that clause requires: by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause, not by a general assertion that traffic was bad.

The excess is exonerated outright under POL-RD-03. The artefact is EV-ADVIS-00111-01, an LTA DataMall CLOSURE on the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Clementi Rd exit' — a segment the booked optimal route uses (the trip record's optimal_route_source is 'BKE southbound then PIE westbound'), so limb (a) is met. Its validity window is 07:10–09:30, bracketing the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip by far more than the 15-minute buffer limb (b) allows, with 41.5 minutes of overlap and overlaps_trip_window true. The 10-second, 100%-coverage trace on EV-GPS-00111 shows the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed segment and rejoining it on the AYE, which is limb (c). All three conditions are satisfied.

The exoneration is not merely partial — it covers the whole measured excess. The POL-RD-03 cap is 1.30 x the ADDITIONAL distance of the shortest lawful alternative over the booked optimal, plus 1.0 km of tolerance: 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km. The measured excess is 5.98 km, which is less than 7.76 km, so justified_excess_km is the measured figure itself and there is no unexonerated residue left for POL-RD-02 to operate on.

The routing is the authority's own diversion, not a discretionary shortcut: the advisory text on EV-ADVIS-00111-01 reads 'Diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd', which is exactly the road the rider's own claim text describes the driver using ('came off at Bukit Panjang and went down Upper Bukit Timah and around by the AYE'). The driver took the published way round a HIGH-severity closure of the corridor the optimal route uses.

Run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal that POL-RD-03 requires — 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, duration scaled from the booked 30.0 min to 37.5 min — and the money simply is not there: recomputed_fare = 3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 37.585, against a charged_total of 37.74. The difference is SGD 0.155, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so under POL-RD-02 read with POL-RD-03 the outcome is NO_ACTION and the charged fare of SGD 37.74 stands as recorded on EV-FARE-00111 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

There is no pass-through correction to add on top. EV-FARE-00111 records tolls_erp 0.00 and an empty erp_gantries list, and the trace crosses no gantry, so the standalone off-route ERP refund that POL-RD-09 gives even an exonerated closure has nothing to operate on and the SGD 12.00 cap on that head is not reached. The distance and time charges stand because POL-RD-03 places the closure beyond the driver's control, and the rider's own claim that he 'did not see any closure' does not put a gantry on the trace.

The chat log confirms the driver told the rider before he diverted — MSG-00111-001, sent 07:54:20, 'boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok' — and the rider read it and answered at 07:54:55, 'as long as i reach by 8.30', without objecting to the route. I do not put this forward as a rider-instructed detour and do not rely on POL-RD-04, because the rider requested no waypoint and waypoint_hint is null; it is offered as contemporaneous notice that corroborates the driver's account of why he left the corridor and rebuts any suggestion the diversion was concealed or self-serving.

No repeat-deviation scrutiny is engaged. POL-RD-06 is triggered only by a MATERIAL deviation — excess over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km absolute, on the excess REMAINING after adjustment — and after the POL-RD-03 cap is applied there is no remaining excess at all, while the raw figures (24.92%, 5.98 km) sit below both materiality thresholds. Were the profile consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 588, which establishes no pattern on the test POL-RD-06 actually states.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties —

The deviation is real. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00111 measures 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km on EV-TRIP-00111, an excess of 5.98 km and 24.9%. That passes both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), and the trace figure governs over the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record. The trace is clean — 229 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gap over 90 seconds and no jump over 500 m — so it is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and the deviation rests on it directly, with no independent-corroboration requirement.

But the driver is not penalised for the detour. The closure is documented by a third-party artifact, EV-ADVIS-00111-01: an LTA DataMall HIGH-severity closure of the PIE towards Tuas after Clementi Rd — a segment the booked optimal route (BKE southbound then PIE westbound) uses — valid 07:10–09:30, which comfortably brackets the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip (41.5 minutes of overlap). The GPS trace shows the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang, before the closed stretch, and rejoining on the AYE; the advisory's own diversion instruction is 'via Upper Bukit Timah Rd', the road the driver actually took. POL-RD-03 limbs (a), (b) and (c) are made out.

The rider's argument that limb (c) fails because the rejoin was on the AYE rather than the PIE is rejected. The clause asks whether the actual route left the optimal corridor before the affected segment and came back to the route to the destination after it; the trace and the platform's own assessment of EV-GPS-00111 show it did, and the AYE is the connecting corridor into one-north, not a further unrelated detour — the advisory's diversion routing leads that way. The rider's statement that he 'did not see any closure' is not evidence against a timestamped, geo-referenced LTA advisory, and the chat log EV-CHAT-00111 shows the driver told him at 07:54:20 and he answered 'as long as i reach by 8.30' without objecting to the route.

The exoneration cap. POL-RD-03 caps the justified excess at min(measured 5.98, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative 29.2 - optimal 24.0) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km. The whole measured excess is therefore justified, and the closure-adjusted optimal is 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, with duration scaled from the booked 30.0 min to 37.5 min (the trip record's amended_optimal_duration_min is null, so the scaled figure governs).

The arithmetic, running POL-RD-02 against that adjusted route:
- charged_total: SGD 37.74 (EV-FARE-00111)
- recomputed_fare: (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0, the 1.0 surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = SGD 37.585
- refund: 37.74 - 37.585 = SGD 0.155, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis.

Outcome. No refund is payable; the outcome is NO_ACTION and the charge stands. On a rider-filed dispute that leaves the fare in place, as POL-GEN-03 provides, and the rider's alternative figure of SGD 6.75 — which would follow only if the exoneration failed — does not arise. There is no pass-through correction under POL-RD-09: tolls_erp is 0.00, erp_gantries is empty and the trace crosses no gantry, so there is nothing to refund under POL-RD-09(2) and no phantom line to refer under POL-RD-09(4).

The chat log is not a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04. Neither message is a rider instruction, both waypoint_hint fields are null and the rider named no road, so the clause's corroboration test cannot be run; as both sides accept, the clause is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. The chat does stand as contemporaneous notice inside the trip window that the driver gave the rider about the closure.

No referral and no escalation. The deviation is not MATERIAL (24.9% and 5.98 km are below the 50% and 8.0 km thresholds), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 588 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern is established and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. No billing-integrity referral arises either. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires: the trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers and timestamps agree across the trip record, trace, fare breakdown and chat, the exculpatory clause has its artifact and every field it requires, the refund is far below SGD 150, and no charge line lacks a counterpart. The rider's bare assertion that he saw no closure is not evidence of comparable strength to a timestamped, geo-referenced LTA advisory, so POL-RD-10(7) is not triggered.

Confidence is 0.9. The decisive facts — the closure, the actual route and the arithmetic — all rest on artifacts whose weight_multiplier is 1.0 (EV-ADVIS-00111-01, EV-GPS-00111, EV-TRIP-00111, EV-FARE-00111), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and nothing here falls below the 0.70 floor.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: this trip did deviate from the booked route, but the driver was entitled to take the way he took because the expressway he would have used was closed, and once that is allowed for the fare works out within a few cents of what was properly chargeable — below the amount the policy treats as worth refunding. The SGD 37.74 charge therefore stands.

WHAT WAS PROVED, AND ON WHICH FIGURE. A deviation is established under POL-RD-01 on the figure that clause makes governing — EV-GPS-00111, trace_distance_km 29.98, not the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on EV-TRIP-00111, which POL-RD-01 forbids citing for the threshold test. The excess over the 24.0 km booked optimal is 5.98 km, or 24.9%. Both gates pass (over 0.8 km and over 20%). The trace itself is clean for policy purposes: 229 fixes at a steady 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 and no straight-line jump, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) does not fire, the trace is admitted, and the rider need not prove the deviation through any independent source.

THE CLOSURE EXONERATES THE WHOLE EXCESS. EV-ADVIS-00111-01 is an LTA DataMall advisory closing the PIE towards Tuas after the Clementi Rd exit from 07:10 to 09:30 — a segment the booked optimal route (BKE southbound then PIE westbound) traverses. It overlaps the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip by 41.5 minutes, far more than the 15-minute buffers limb (b) allows. The trace shows the vehicle leaving the corridor at Bukit Panjang, before the closed segment, and rejoining after it, taking the diversion the advisory itself publishes ('Diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd'). On the rider's point that nothing returns the vehicle to the PIE corridor: limb (c) asks whether the actual route leaves before the affected segment and rejoins after, and the trace shows it did, along the authority's own diversion. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met.

THE CAP DOES NOT BITE. The POL-RD-03 cap is 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km. The measured excess of 5.98 km is below it, so the justified excess is the whole 5.98 km and the closure-adjusted optimal is 29.98 km over 37.5 minutes.

THE ARITHMETIC, ON SEPARATE LINES (POL-RD-02 run against the closure-adjusted optimal, as POL-RD-03 requires):
- charged_total: SGD 37.74
- recomputed_fare: (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 (the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00111) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = SGD 37.585
- refund: SGD 0.155
That is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is NO_ACTION. The rider's alternative computation against the booked 24 km optimal (recomputed_fare SGD 31.00, refund SGD 6.75) is not used, because the closure exoneration is made out on the record.

PASS-THROUGHS AND CONDUCT. tolls_erp is 0.00, erp_gantries is empty and the trace crosses no gantry, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to settle and there is no billing-integrity finding or referral. The deviation is not MATERIAL (24.9% and 5.98 km are below both 50% and 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral arises; were the profile consulted it shows deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 588, which establishes no pattern. The chat log (the driver's 07:54:20 notice that the PIE was closed and that he was coming off at Bukit Panjang, and the rider's reply without objection) supports the driver's account of why he left the corridor. It is not a rider-requested detour — waypoint_hint is null on both messages — and neither side relies on POL-RD-04, so no part of the excess is excluded on that footing and no driver compensation is payable on the distance billed (30.0 km charged against a 29.98 km trace is not a shortfall).

NO ESCALATION. The trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00111, EV-GPS-00111 and EV-FARE-00111, no timestamps disagree or run backwards, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or off-window artifact, the refund is nowhere near SGD 150, and there is no contradiction of comparable strength — the rider's recollection of not seeing a closure does not weigh against an official LTA advisory. Confidence is 0.90; every artifact carrying the deciding facts (the advisory, the trace and the trip record) sits at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0.

Because the refundable difference is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands: the SGD 37.74 charge is left as recorded (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and nothing is owed to the driver.

It overlaps the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip by 41.5 minutes, far more than the 15-minute buffers limb (b) allows. The trace shows the vehicle leaving the corridor at Bukit Panjang, before the closed segment, and rejoining after it, taking the diversion the advisory itself publishes ('Diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd'). On the rider's point that nothing returns the vehicle to the PIE corridor: limb (c) asks whether the actual route leaves before the affected segment and rejoins after, and the trace shows it did, along the authority's own diversion. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met.

THE CAP DOES NOT BITE. The POL-RD-03 cap is 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km. The measured excess of 5.98 km is below it, so the justified excess is the whole 5.98 km and the closure-adjusted optimal is 29.98 km over 37.5 minutes.

THE ARITHMETIC, ON SEPARATE LINES (POL-RD-02 run against the closure-adjusted optimal, as POL-RD-03 requires):
- charged_total: SGD 37.74
- recomputed_fare: (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 (the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00111) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = SGD 37.585
- refund: SGD 0.155
That is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is NO_ACTION. The rider's alternative computation against the booked 24 km optimal (recomputed_fare SGD 31.00, refund SGD 6.75) is not used, because the closure exoneration is made out on the record.

PASS-THROUGHS AND CONDUCT. tolls_erp is 0.00, erp_gantries is empty and the trace crosses no gantry, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to settle and there is no billing-integrity finding or referral. The deviation is not MATERIAL (24.9% and 5.98 km are below both 50% and 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral arises; were the profile consulted it shows deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 588, which establishes no pattern. The chat log (the driver's 07:54:20 notice that the PIE was closed and that he was coming off at Bukit Panjang, and the rider's reply without objection) supports the driver's account of why he left the corridor. It is not a rider-requested detour — waypoint_hint is null on both messages — and neither side relies on POL-RD-04, so no part of the excess is excluded on that footing and no driver compensation is payable on the distance billed (30.0 km charged against a 29.98 km trace is not a shortfall).

NO ESCALATION. The trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00111, EV-GPS-00111 and EV-FARE-00111, no timestamps disagree or run backwards, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or off-window artifact, the refund is nowhere near SGD 150, and there is no contradiction of comparable strength — the rider's recollection of not seeing a closure does not weigh against an official LTA advisory. Confidence is 0.90; every artifact carrying the deciding facts (the advisory, the trace and the trip record) sits at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0.

Because the refundable difference is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands: the SGD 37.74 charge is left as recorded (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and nothing is owed to the driver."

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver — the trip's own telemetry decides this, and the fare that was charged stands.

The deviation is real. Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is the GPS trace, not the rounded copy on the trip record: EV-GPS-00111 records 29.98 km (trace_distance_km) against the booked optimal of 24.0 km on EV-TRIP-00111, an excess of 5.98 km and 24.9%. Both gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%) are crossed, and the 29.98 km figure governs over the 30.0 km convenience copy, as POL-RD-01 requires. The rider's threshold showing under POL-RD-08 is made out.

That excess is nevertheless exonerated in full under POL-RD-03. EV-ADVIS-00111-01 is a HIGH-severity LTA DataMall closure of the PIE towards Tuas after the Clementi Rd exit — a segment the booked optimal route (BKE southbound then PIE westbound) uses; its window of 07:10–09:30 brackets the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip with 41.5 minutes of overlap, far beyond the 15-minute buffer; and the unbroken trace shows the vehicle leaving the corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed stretch and rejoining it after, via the advisory's own designated diversion, Upper Bukit Timah Rd. The cap works as follows: 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km, and the measured excess of 5.98 km is within it, so the whole excess is justified and no distance or time refund survives.

The rider's argument that the rejoin limb fails because the vehicle rejoined on the AYE rather than the PIE is rejected. The clause asks whether the actual route left the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoined it after; the 229-fix, 100%-coverage trace on EV-GPS-00111 shows exactly that, and the expressway network is re-entered on the AYE, which serves the destination at one-north. The driver did what the authority's advisory told road users to do, and POL-RD-03 exists so that a driver who correctly avoids a closed expressway is not penalised for it.

On the money, run against the closure-adjusted optimal that POL-RD-03 requires: charged_total is SGD 37.74 (EV-FARE-00111); recomputed_fare is SGD 37.585 (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP); refund is SGD 0.155. That is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is NO_ACTION. The rider's alternative computation of SGD 6.75 rests on running POL-RD-02 against the unadjusted 24.0 km optimal and so does not apply once the closure is taken into account.

POL-RD-09 adds nothing: EV-FARE-00111 records tolls_erp of 0.00 and an empty erp_gantries list, and the trace crosses no gantry, so there is no off-route or phantom ERP charge to refund and no billing-integrity referral arises. POL-RD-04 does not excuse any part of the detour — the chat contains no rider instruction to take a particular road and both waypoint_hint fields are null, so its corroboration test cannot be run — but nothing turns on it, since the driver does not rely on it and the closure exonerates the route in full. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: after the adjustment no excess remains, and even the raw figures (24.9%, 5.98 km) are below the materiality thresholds of 50% and 8.0 km; on the profile, deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 588 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no driver-conduct referral is produced. No profile field is used as a ground of decision (POL-GEN-01): the rider's deviation_claims_60d of 1 is below POL-RD-08's threshold of 4, and ratings, account ages and lifetime counters are context only.

NO_ACTION is party-relative. The SGD 37.74 already charged stands and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00; the charge was live (payment_status CHARGED), and it is left in place because the evidence does not support a refund, not because the rider's account was disbelieved — the LTA advisory answers the rider's 'I did not see any closure'. The driver receives no compensation: the fare billed 30.0 km against a trace of 29.98 km, so there is no unbilled distance to pay for under POL-RD-04. The driver's chat message sent at 07:54:20 is accepted as contemporaneous notice of the closure, though the advisory already carries that fact.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the fare of SGD 37.74 stands, and no refund is due. This is not a driver taking a route of his own choosing — the record shows he followed a published road closure diversion.

EV-ADVIS-00111-01 is an LTA DataMall closure on the Pan Island Expressway towards Tuas, the corridor the platform's optimal route (BKE southbound then PIE westbound) uses: a HIGH-severity vehicle fire, all lanes closed between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit, valid 07:10–09:30 — which brackets the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip with far more than the 15-minute buffer — overlapping 41.5 minutes, intersecting the route, and diverting traffic via Upper Bukit Timah Rd. That is exactly the road the driver used.

POL-RD-03 is satisfied on all three limbs. (a) The advisory names a segment the optimal route traverses. (b) Its window overlaps the trip. (c) The trace on EV-GPS-00111 — 229 fixes at a steady 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — shows the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang, before the closed segment, and rejoining it on the AYE on the final run-in to the booked drop-off at one-north. On the rider's point that the rejoin is on the AYE rather than the PIE: the AYE is the destination-side approach to one-north, and the leave-before / rejoin-after pattern the clause requires is present on the trace; the driver also told the rider in-app at 07:54:20 that the PIE was closed and that he was coming off at Bukit Panjang, and the rider did not object.

The exoneration is capped, and the cap does not bite: 1.30 × (29.2 − 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km against a measured excess of 5.98 km, so the whole excess is justified and no deviation remains under POL-RD-01. Running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route (29.98 km, 37.5 min) gives a recomputed fare of SGD 37.585 against SGD 37.74 charged — SGD 0.155, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so nothing issues. The SGD 6.75 figure the rider's advocate computes is the booked-route calculation, and it does not apply once the closure is accounted for.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m, no sampling interval above 30 s), so no escalation arises on that head. POL-RD-04 is not engaged — no rider instructed the detour, waypoint_hint is null on both chat messages, and the driver's exoneration rests on POL-RD-03 alone; the chat log is contemporaneous notice, not a detour request. POL-RD-09 has nothing to settle: tolls_erp is 0.00, erp_gantries is empty, neither route crosses a gantry at this hour, and there is no unmatched charge line and so no billing-integrity defect. POL-RD-06 is not engaged: this is not a material deviation, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 588 completed trips, so there is no pattern and no conduct referral. The rider's statement that he saw no closure is a bare assertion and does not outweigh the transport authority's own advisory. The party profiles were used only as context in accordance with POL-GEN-01.

ledger.claim: The trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation measured on the figure POL-RD-01 makes governing: EV-GPS-00111 records a trace of 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km, an excess of 5.98 km and 24.9%. Both gates are crossed - the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms - and the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record is expressly not the field the threshold test runs on.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 229 fixes at a steady 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 and no straight-line jump between consecutive fixes. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and the rider is not put to proving it through any independent source.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00111, agree on the 07:47:40 pickup event, and the excess crosses the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden has accordingly shifted to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; a general assertion that the PIE was bad that morning does not discharge it.

The rider's own record does not trigger the POL-RD-08 additional-corroboration rule: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0. That factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven, and under POL-GEN-01 no other field on the rider profile bears on this test at all.

POL-RD-04 cannot excuse any part of this detour. The chat log contains only the driver's own notification - 'i come off at bukit panjang ok', sent at 07:54:20, after he had already left the optimal corridor - and the rider's 'as long as i reach by 8.30'. Neither message is a rider instruction to take a particular road, both waypoint_hint fields are null, and the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 therefore cannot be run at all. Acquiescence in a decision the driver had already taken is not a rider-requested detour.

The driver's closure defence exonerates only if every limb of POL-RD-03 is made out, and the third limb is not established on this record: the actual route must leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment AND rejoin it after. The record places the rejoin on the AYE, while the trip_record describes the optimal route as the BKE southbound then the PIE westbound; no artifact puts the vehicle back on that corridor after the closure. The driver carries the burden under POL-RD-08, and on the face of the artifacts he has not shown the rejoin the clause requires, so the excess is not exonerated and falls to be refunded.

If the exoneration is not made out, the money is arithmetic and not discretionary. Against the booked optimal route, recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP and zero fixed surcharges = 31.00; charged_total was 37.74, so the refund is 6.74, payable rounded up to SGD 6.75. That is 17.9% of the amount charged, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the rider's entitlement on these figures is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

The disputed charge is live and not already settled: the fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so anything short of a refund, or of an escalation that holds the sum, leaves the rider carrying the disputed SGD 8.00. A NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute is party-relative and is not a neutral outcome for this rider.

The threshold showing is made out on this trip and nowhere else. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00111 and agree on the pickup/start at 2026-08-03T07:47:40+08:00, so POL-RD-08(a) is satisfied; and on the trace figure that governs under POL-RD-01 (trace_distance_km 29.98, not the rounded actual_distance_km 30.0) the excess over the booked optimal of 24.0 km is 5.98 km and 24.92% — past both the 0.8 km and the 20% gates. The burden therefore shifts to the driver under POL-RD-08, and the driver discharges it the way that clause requires: by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause, not by a general assertion that traffic was bad.

The excess is exonerated outright under POL-RD-03. The artefact is EV-ADVIS-00111-01, an LTA DataMall CLOSURE on the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Clementi Rd exit' — a segment the booked optimal route uses (the trip record's optimal_route_source is 'BKE southbound then PIE westbound'), so limb (a) is met. Its validity window is 07:10–09:30, bracketing the 07:47:40–08:25:40 trip by far more than the 15-minute buffer limb (b) allows, with 41.5 minutes of overlap and overlaps_trip_window true. The 10-second, 100%-coverage trace on EV-GPS-00111 shows the vehicle leaving the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed segment and rejoining it on the AYE, which is limb (c). All three conditions are satisfied.

The exoneration is not merely partial — it covers the whole measured excess. The POL-RD-03 cap is 1.30 x the ADDITIONAL distance of the shortest lawful alternative over the booked optimal, plus 1.0 km of tolerance: 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00 = 7.76 km. The measured excess is 5.98 km, which is less than 7.76 km, so justified_excess_km is the measured figure itself and there is no unexonerated residue left for POL-RD-02 to operate on.

The routing is the authority's own diversion, not a discretionary shortcut: the advisory text on EV-ADVIS-00111-01 reads 'Diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd', which is exactly the road the rider's own claim text describes the driver using ('came off at Bukit Panjang and went down Upper Bukit Timah and around by the AYE'). The driver took the published way round a HIGH-severity closure of the corridor the optimal route uses.

Run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal that POL-RD-03 requires — 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, duration scaled from the booked 30.0 min to 37.5 min — and the money simply is not there: recomputed_fare = 3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 37.585, against a charged_total of 37.74. The difference is SGD 0.155, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so under POL-RD-02 read with POL-RD-03 the outcome is NO_ACTION and the charged fare of SGD 37.74 stands as recorded on EV-FARE-00111 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

There is no pass-through correction to add on top. EV-FARE-00111 records tolls_erp 0.00 and an empty erp_gantries list, and the trace crosses no gantry, so the standalone off-route ERP refund that POL-RD-09 gives even an exonerated closure has nothing to operate on and the SGD 12.00 cap on that head is not reached. The distance and time charges stand because POL-RD-03 places the closure beyond the driver's control, and the rider's own claim that he 'did not see any closure' does not put a gantry on the trace.

The chat log confirms the driver told the rider before he diverted — MSG-00111-001, sent 07:54:20, 'boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok' — and the rider read it and answered at 07:54:55, 'as long as i reach by 8.30', without objecting to the route. I do not put this forward as a rider-instructed detour and do not rely on POL-RD-04, because the rider requested no waypoint and waypoint_hint is null; it is offered as contemporaneous notice that corroborates the driver's account of why he left the corridor and rebuts any suggestion the diversion was concealed or self-serving.

No repeat-deviation scrutiny is engaged. POL-RD-06 is triggered only by a MATERIAL deviation — excess over 50% of optimal or over 8.0 km absolute, on the excess REMAINING after adjustment — and after the POL-RD-03 cap is applied there is no remaining excess at all, while the raw figures (24.92%, 5.98 km) sit below both materiality thresholds. Were the profile consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 588, which establishes no pattern on the test POL-RD-06 actually states.
